title: Elastic Translations: Fast Virtual Memory with Multiple Translation Sizes
problem: Virtual memory translation overhead limits performance despite ARM and RISC-V supporting intermediate translation sizes (64KiB, 32MiB); existing OS lack efficient mechanisms to exploit these sizes due to limited coalescing support and runtime selection strategies.
motivation: Efficient use of multiple translation sizes can significantly reduce TLB misses and translation overhead, directly improving performance of memory-intensive workloads.
method: Elastic Translations (ET) implements coalescing-aware OS memory manager mechanisms to transparently select among multiple translation sizes at runtime. It uses lightweight hardware-assisted TLB miss sampling to guide translation size selection policies. The system dynamically adapts page sizes based on observed memory access patterns and is implemented for ARMv8-A in Linux and KVM.
key_novelty: Hardware-assisted TLB miss sampling integrated with runtime translation size selection policies to dynamically exploit intermediate translation sizes without requiring static large-page configurations.
contributions: Coalescing-aware OS memory manager mechanisms enabling transparent use of multiple translation sizes
Lightweight hardware-assisted TLB miss sampling for runtime page size selection
Full implementation for ARMv8-A in Linux and KVM supporting native and virtualized execution
Performance improvements up to 39% in native execution and 30% average in virtualized workloads

metrics.speedup: up to 39% native execution, 30% average virtualized execution

limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations in the abstract.
